stories.title: Indian Restaurant Samudhra Takes 10K SF at 312 West 43rd Street
stories.excerpt: New Jersey-based Indian restaurant Samudhra is establishing a presence across the Hudson River in Hell’s Kitchen. The eatery signed a 10,000-square-foot lease on the ground level of the Ellery at 312 West 43rd Street, owned by Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors, for its second location in the U.S. following its first restaurant in Franklin Park, N.J., according to the landlords. Taconic did not disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease, but asking rent for prime retail space in the nearby Times Square retail corridor of Broadway and Seventh Avenue from 42nd to 47th streets was $1,400 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood,” George Tsapelas, senior vice president of Taconic, said in a statement. “From the outset, our vision for the Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area, and Samudhra further strengthens the retail and dining mix we’ve curated at the property.” CBRE’s Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh and Bevan Cohen negotiated on behalf of the landlord while Brad Schwarz from Lee & Associates handled the deal for the tenant. CBRE and Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The Ellery provides an exceptional setting for our New York City location and gives us the opportunity to introduce our distinctive premium Indian dining and lounge experience to a much broader audience,” Mangesh Chinthamaneni, founder and CEO at Samudhra, said in a statement. The announcement comes almost exactly a year after German grocery chain Aldi signed a lease spanning 25,000 square feet on the ground floor of the building in late August 2025 as part of Aldi’s broader rollout across the U.S. The New York Post first reported Samudhra’s lease deal. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Samudhra Indian restaurant leases 10K SF ground floor at 312 West 43rd Street, Hell's Kitchen.
Prime Times Square retail asking rents at $1,400/SF in Q2 2026; mixed-use Ellery anchored by restaurant tenant.
Retail activation signals continued Hell's Kitchen demand but limited direct multifamily development signal.
stories.summary: New Jersey-based Samudhra restaurant signed a 10,000-square-foot ground-floor lease at the Ellery (312 West 43rd Street) in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan, marking its second U.S. location. The deal anchors a mixed-use building owned by Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors. Prime retail rents in the nearby Times Square corridor (Broadway/Seventh Avenue, 42nd–47th Street) stood at $1,400/SF in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Ground-floor retail activation at mixed-use developments reinforces foot traffic and resident amenity value in Hell's Kitchen, but this lease alone carries limited forward demand signal for multifamily developers; the real signal is sustained retail momentum and neighborhood vibrancy underpinning existing and future residential inventory in Midtown West.

stories.title: East Harlem Housing Proposal on City-Owned Lot Expands to 762 Units
stories.excerpt: An affordable and supportive housing complex slated for a city-owned site in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood just got 62 units larger. The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) submitted plans on Friday to rezone the city block surrounding 22 East 119th Street. The requested amendments will facilitate a housing project spanning three buildings with a total of 762 units. PincusCo first reported on the filing. The site is currently occupied by a six-story, 174-unit single room occupancy building where Volunteers of America–Greater New York hosts supportive housing for formerly homeless, single adults, many of whom are veterans. In accordance with a city policy that avoids “spot zoning” individual tax lots, the rezoning proposal would impact the entire East Harlem block, bounded by East 118th and East 119th streets, between Madison and Fifth avenues. In addition to the site’s designation as an urban renewal area and the disposition of city-owned property, HPD’s requested amendments would label the block as a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area, ensuring affordable housing will be a part of any future redevelopments of the block’s privately owned buildings. A prior iteration of the project, sponsored by nonprofit Volunteers of America–Greater New York, planned 700 units across two buildings. Those included a 23-story supportive housing tower and a 25-story affordable housing tower. Plans also incorporated community space and commercial facilities for the nonprofit, with funding sought through HPD and the New York City Housing Development Corporation. Land use documents accompanying the newest proposal at 22 East 119th Street are not currently available. The change in site plans, and how surrounding buildings or project timelines will be impacted, is unclear. bullets: HPD expands East Harlem 22 East 119th Street project to 762 units across three buildings (+62 units).
City-owned site rezoning affects entire block (E. 118th–119th, Madison–Fifth Ave); mixed affordable/supportive housing.
Urban renewal area and public disposition reduce private capital requirement; supply addition in high-demand East Harlem submarket.
stories.summary: The NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development filed a rezoning request for the block surrounding 22 East 119th Street in East Harlem to facilitate a 762-unit affordable and supportive housing complex spanning three buildings. The site currently holds a 174-unit single-room occupancy building operated by Volunteers of America for formerly homeless single adults. The rezoning affects the entire block bounded by East 118th and 119th streets between Madison and Fifth avenues to avoid spot-zoning.
stories.impact: Public sector supply of 762 units in East Harlem (a high-demand, gentrifying submarket) will absorb considerable affordable-housing demand, potentially constraining market-rate rental pricing power and reducing absorption velocity for nearby private multifamily developments in Manhattan's East Harlem and Upper East Side submarkets over the next 3–5 years.

stories.title: Green Point Building 754K-SF Georgetown Spec Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Green Point Property plans to build a 754,000-square-foot spec building in Georgetown that could eventually have 3 million square feet of industrial space. It’s in the GTX Logistics Park at 1000 FM 972 The building costs are estimated at $42 million for the concrete tilt-wall warehouse shell that is scheduled to begin construction in October and be completed in November 2027. The Austin Business Journal reports the GTX Logistics Park is marketing 2.6 million square feet left on the 180 acres it still owns. Colliers International Group Inc.’s Travis Hicks and Chase Clancy handle leasing at the site. Georgetown is about 30 miles north of Austin with a population of nearly 107,000 people. Gree Point says its focus is on high-growth markets throughout Texas and the Southeastern US to acquire and develop industrial properties. Green Point’s team has 40 years of combined real estate investment experience and collectively has acquired, developed and managed real estate assets exceeding $3 billion across the United States. The post Green Point Building 754K-SF Georgetown Spec Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Green Point builds 754K-SF spec warehouse in Georgetown, Texas (30 miles north of Austin); $42M estimated cost.
GTX Logistics Park (180 acres) has 2.6M SF available; construction starts Oct 2026, completes Nov 2027.
Industrial supply addition signals strong Austin-area logistics demand but does not directly impact multifamily.
stories.summary: Green Point Property is developing a 754,000-square-foot spec warehouse at GTX Logistics Park (1000 FM 972) in Georgetown, Texas, north of Austin, with an estimated cost of $42 million. Construction is scheduled to begin in October 2026 and complete in November 2027. The 180-acre park still has 2.6 million square feet available for lease, and Green Point focuses on high-growth Texas and Southeast markets.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact; this is industrial supply. However, logistics infrastructure expansion in Georgetown/Austin corridor supports job growth and inbound migration that will eventually drive multifamily demand; developers should monitor GTX Logistics Park tenant announcements and tenant workforce composition for secondary demand signals in greater Austin metro.

stories.title: Truist Lends $277M on Jersey City Multifamily Tower Build
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Rockpoint and Urby has secured $277 million of construction financing to develop the second phase of a multifamily tower in Jersey City, Commercial Observer has learned. Truist provided the loan for the sponsorship’s 748-unit 201 Hudson – by Urby project along the Jersey City waterfront. Rockpoint and Ubry joined forces to acquire land at 201 Hudson Street for the project in July, CO first reported at the time. “This financing reflects Truist’s continued commitment to supporting premier sponsors pursuing transformative multifamily developments in high-growth urban markets,” said Rebecca M. Cox, senior vice president and market manager at Truist National Real Estate. The transaction was led by Katie Kennedy, Northeast market leader at Truist, with Walt Reece, a director of real estate syndicated finance at Truist Securities, leading the syndication, according to the firm. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Chris Kramer, Holden Witkoff and Jack Fenton. The brokerage firm also advised the joint venture partners on the joint venture capitalization with a team composed of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Michael Collins. Located in Jersey City’s Paulus Hook neighborhood, 201 Hudson – by Urby marks the second phase of a 69-story tower that will include 528,000 rentable square feet and 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Community amenities will include a pool, a fitness center and coworking spaces. Rockpoint, Urby and Newmark did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Truist funds $277M construction loan for Rockpoint–Urby 748-unit tower at 201 Hudson, Jersey City waterfront.
Joint venture acquired land July 2025; financing reflects strong capital availability for premier urban multifamily.
High-growth urban coastal market (Jersey City) continues to attract major sponsor equity and institutional debt.
stories.summary: Rockpoint and Urby secured $277 million in construction financing from Truist for the second phase of 201 Hudson—a 748-unit multifamily tower in Jersey City. The joint venture acquired the waterfront land in July 2025. Truist emphasized continued commitment to premier sponsors pursuing transformative developments in high-growth urban markets. Newmark negotiated the debt transaction.
stories.impact: Strong construction financing availability and lender appetite for institutional multifamily in Jersey City waterfront signals sustained investor confidence in Northeast urban rental markets; for developers, this validates competitive acquisition and underwriting timelines in Jersey City submarket and suggests debt terms remain favorable for transit-adjacent, mixed-use urban projects through 2027.

stories.title: Houston Office Building Owners Ink $250M Refi
stories.excerpt: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital secured a $250 million CMBS loan to refinance 777 Hidden Ridge, a 1.1 million-square-foot office property in Irving, Texas. Commercial Search reports that Bank of America originated the two-year, interest-only note with three one-year extension options. Previous debt includes a $253.8 million note issued by Citizens Financial Group in 2019, set to mature in 2029. KDC and Verizon completed the building in 2019, developed on a build-to-suit basis for Pioneer Natural Resources USA Inc. That same year, PRP and Riyad acquired the asset. Pioneer had inked a 20-year, triple-net lease set to run until 2039. The agreement has no early termination and no contractual rights for the remainder of the term. Pioneer has since left the building, but must fulfill the lease obligations. Pioneer is looking to sublease the space. The 10-story building has amenities such as a conference center, gym, coffee shop, on-site childcare, medical clinic and six-story parking garage with 2,569 spaces. The post Houston Office Building Owners Ink $250M Refi appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital refinance 777 Hidden Ridge (Irving, TX; 1.1M SF office) with $250M CMBS loan.
Pioneer Natural Resources vacated but remains obligated on 20-year NNN lease (expires 2039); sublease underway.
Office refinancing amid tenant departure indicates asset-level stress, not multifamily-relevant; provides no demand signal.
stories.summary: PRP Real Assets and Riyad Capital secured a $250 million CMBS loan to refinance 777 Hidden Ridge, a 1.1 million-square-foot office building in Irving, Texas, developed in 2019 on a build-to-suit for Pioneer Natural Resources. The two-year interest-only note includes three one-year extension options and refinances $253.8 million of prior debt from Citizens Financial Group. Pioneer has vacated but remains liable on the 20-year triple-net lease through 2039 and is seeking sublease tenants.
stories.impact: Not relevant to multifamily development; this is distressed office asset management. The article signals office oversupply and tenant mobility in Irving/DFW, which indirectly supports multifamily demand if displaced office workers seek alternative work-from-home or flexible workspace, but this is speculative and sector-agnostic.

stories.title: VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community
stories.excerpt: VIC Partners obtained a $36.5 million primary line of credit for the construction of Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing development at 7120 Anderson Blvd. in Fort Worth outside of Loop 820 and north of Interstate 30. The project is being developed by Vic Partners and M-13 Construction. OakNorth Bank will provide the loan as part of a $48 million joint financing with Hickory CRE Capital, a commercial real estate lender. Concord Summit Capital arranged the construction loan. VIC suggests the cost of the construction will be $41.7 million. The development will consist of nine three-story residential buildings, a clubhouse, fitness center, pickleball court and business center along with 402 parking spaces.  The post VIC Partners Obtains Construction Loan for 268-Unit FW Workforce Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: VIC Partners secures $36.5M primary credit line (+ $48M joint facility with Hickory CRE) for Vic Centre, Fort Worth.
268-unit workforce-housing development at 7120 Anderson Blvd (north of I-30, outside Loop 820); $41.7M hard costs.
OakNorth and Hickory CRE provide construction debt; development by Vic Partners and M-13 Construction.
stories.summary: VIC Partners obtained a $36.5 million primary line of credit from OakNorth Bank as part of a $48 million joint financing facility (with Hickory CRE Capital) for Vic Centre, a 268-unit workforce-housing development in Fort Worth. The project, located at 7120 Anderson Boulevard north of I-30 and outside Loop 820, will feature nine three-story residential buildings with amenities and 402 parking spaces. Construction cost is estimated at $41.7 million.
stories.impact: Workforce-housing construction financing in Fortworth demonstrates lender appetite for affordable/workforce multifamily in secondary Texas metros; the project's location (outer Loop 820) signals developers' focus on expanding supply in suburban growth corridors where land and construction costs support workforce rents—expect continued supply concentration in north Fort Worth submarkets.

stories.title: W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa
stories.excerpt: W Properties plans to build a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on approximately 12 acres adjacent to Everbloom (shown), the company’s 343-unit build-to-rent community in Melissa, Texas. The company said it’s taking a different approach with garden-style apartments, a sector still working through elevated supply and concessions across North Texas. Texas multifamily permitting across its five major metros has fallen by more than half from its 2023 peak, while Dallas-Fort Worth continues to absorb a significant pipeline of apartments already under construction. W Properties Andrew Welker added, “BTR and garden-style apartments are different products, and we would not have started a garden-style project in that same environment. We expect to go vertical by mid-2027, positioning this community for an early 2029 leasing season, when we believe today’s supply pressure will look materially different.” The post W Properties Mixing BTR and Garden-Style Apartments in Melissa appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: W Properties plans 252-unit garden-style community on 12 acres in Melissa, Texas adjacent to 343-unit BTR Everbloom.
Texas multifamily permitting down >50% from 2023 peak; DFW absorbing heavy pipeline; vertical start mid-2027.
Delayed timing (early 2029 lease-up) reflects developer conviction that supply pressure will ease; compressed permitting supports future rents.
stories.summary: W Properties plans to develop a 252-unit garden-style multifamily community on approximately 12 acres in Melissa, Texas, adjacent to its 343-unit Everbloom build-to-rent community. The developer stated it would not have started a garden-style project in the current oversupplied environment and plans to break ground mid-2027, targeting early 2029 leasing. Texas multifamily permitting across its five major metros has fallen more than 50% from its 2023 peak, while Dallas–Fort Worth continues absorbing a substantial pipeline of apartments already under construction.
stories.impact: Sharp permitting decline (>50% year-over-year) and developer decision to delay garden-style starts until 2029 signal market inflection: elevated concessions and supply pressure are expected to clear by early 2029, suggesting DFW rents will recover and new starts will accelerate once existing pipeline stabilizes; developers should monitor Dallas–Fort Worth absorption metrics and concession trends closely through 2028 to time ground breaks for 2030+ leasing seasons.

stories.title: REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit
stories.excerpt: REITs posted record highs for funds from operations (FFO) and net operating income (NOI) in 2026’s second quarter while maintaining strong balance sheets, according to Nareit’s latest REIT Industry Tracker. More than 70% of REITs reported year-over-year increases in FFO, while nearly 80% reported year-over-year increases in NOI. Industry Tracker data show that FFO reached $22.4 billion in Q2, up 12.4% Y-O-Y. Meanwhile, NOI reached $32.7 billion, up 6.8%. Additionally, same-store NOI experienced a 4.1% Y-O-Y gain, demonstrating that REIT operations outpaced inflation in the second quarter, which was 3.5% “The strength we’re seeing from the REIT industry isn’t coming from one measure or sector,” said John Worth, EVP of research & investor outreach at Nareit. “Across the board, REITs continue to generate strong income from their properties reflecting rising occupancy while maintaining robust balance sheets. That combination speaks to the underlying resilience of the industry amid ongoing economic uncertainty.” The post REITs Post Record High FFO in Q2 2026: Nareit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nareit reports REITs hit record FFO ($22.4B, +12.4% YoY) and NOI ($32.7B, +6.8% YoY) in Q2 2026.
>70% REITs posted FFO gains; ~80% posted NOI gains; same-store NOI +4.1% YoY (outpaced 3.5% inflation).
Strong balance sheets and occupancy gains underscore sector resilience; no sector-specific multifamily detail provided.
stories.summary: REITs posted record FFO of $22.4 billion (up 12.4% year-over-year) and NOI of $32.7 billion (up 6.8%) in Q2 2026, according to Nareit's Industry Tracker. Over 70% of REITs reported year-over-year FFO increases, while nearly 80% reported NOI gains. Same-store NOI grew 4.1% year-over-year, outpacing the 2.5% inflation rate and reflecting rising occupancy and strong operational performance.
stories.impact: Record REIT FFO and NOI growth, combined with robust balance sheets and occupancy gains, signals strong institutional capital availability and investor appetite for multifamily acquisitions and refinancings; for developers, this validates favorable debt and equity markets through 2027, supporting aggressive underwriting and acquisition timelines for development platforms seeking JV or equity partnerships with REIT sponsors.

stories.title: Mamdani Sets Sights on Fixing — Not Replacing — Deteriorating Section of BQE
stories.excerpt: Will Mayor Zohran Mamdani be the first administration to finally fix the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) along Brooklyn Heights? Mamdani announced Monday morning that the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) would build bypasses around the surrounding neighborhoods and maintain access to local attractions while finally rebuilding the swiftly deteriorating cantilever portion of the freeway. DOT would build a two-level bypass above Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, sitting below the promenade and not extending above the current highway. The city would also create a second elevated bypass from Columbia Heights to the Manhattan Bridge. The Mamdani administration plans to start the estimated $4 billion project in 2030, despite a sense of urgency from officials. The city estimates the project could take 10 years. The Mamdani administration said it believes this renovation, as opposed to a replacement, will extend the life of the BQE for another 40 years. “After decades of kicking the can down the road and indecision that failed to yield substantial results, we will act with urgency to rehabilitate the city’s portion of the BQE to ensure the safety of New Yorkers and minimize the likelihood of massive traffic diversions into Brooklyn neighborhoods,” DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn said in a statement. “While the city and the state must right the wrongs of Robert Moses with the BQE and other infrastructure plowed through urban communities, decades of political paralysis have left us out of options.” For every year that the city procrastinates, costs increase by an estimated $160 million, according to the announcement. “For decades, prior administrations have failed to deliver urgent long-term repairs to BQE Central — but we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution,” Mamdani said in a statement. “We’re going to fix the aging concrete, repair the deteriorating triple cantilever and build temporary roads that keep the highway operabl
bullets: NYC DOT plans $4B BQE repair project (not replacement) starting 2030; estimated 10-year timeline.
Two-level bypass above Furman Street (Atlantic to Columbia Heights); second elevated bypass to Manhattan Bridge.
Infrastructure project carries indirect benefit to Brooklyn waterfront and heights multifamily via improved access/vitality.
stories.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a $4 billion Department of Transportation plan to repair (rather than fully replace) the deteriorating cantilever section of the Brooklyn–Queens Expressway (BQE). The project includes two elevated bypasses to maintain neighborhood access and local attraction connectivity while rebuilding the freeway structure. Construction is estimated to begin in 2030 and take approximately 10 years, with the city projecting the repairs will extend the BQE's life another 40 years.
stories.impact: BQE infrastructure investment improves long-term accessibility and neighborhood vitality in Brooklyn Heights, DUMBO, and surrounding waterfront submarkets; however, the 2030–2040 construction timeline and extended project duration may create near-term traffic disruption and noise, potentially dampening multifamily leasing and rent growth in adjacent Brooklyn Heights and DUMBO through 2032, offsetting long-term infrastructure upside.

stories.title: Kinsmen Property Group Plans to Bring 322 New Homes to 156-166 Bowery
stories.excerpt: Kinsmen Property Group, a New York City-based real estate development and investment firm, has big plans to build 322 homes along the Bowery in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. After previously filing plans to demolish a 15,000-square-foot set of vacant buildings at 156-166 Bowery in October 2024, Kinsmen has now filed a land use application with the Department of City Planning to transform the now-vacant lot into three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings with a total of 322 homes, according to the firm. If approved, the three buildings would comprise a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors; a 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 3,260 square feet of ground-floor retail space; and another 26-story building with 99 mixed-income units and 4,391 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The project, which would be designed by architects Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter public review through a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) by the end of the year. “We are excited to bring more than 300 new homes to Lower Manhattan at a time when housing is urgently needed across the city,” Ari Zagdanski, principal of Kinsmen, said in a statement. “This project is designed to honor the rich history of the Bowery while also addressing the city’s housing needs head-on.” The site at 156-166 Bowery has already been through various different planned projects. In 2022, previous owner Real Estate Equities Corporation (REEC) — which had signed a 99-year ground lease for the properties in 2020 for $50 million — filed plans to construct a seven-story, 73,000-square-foot retail and office building on the site. Construction on that project eventually stalled. It’s unclear whether REEC still owns the ground lease at the Nolita site, which Kinsmen bought in a set of separate purchases in 2016 and 2017 for a total of $53.5 million, according to records. bullets: Kinsmen Property Group plans 322-unit mixed-income complex at 156–166 Bowery, Nolita (Manhattan); three towers.
29-story building (124 affordable senior units) + two 26-story buildings (99 mixed-income units each + retail); ULURP by EOY.
Manhattan Nolita micromarket adding significant supply; architects KPF and Beyer Blinder Belle; design/entitlement phase.
stories.summary: Kinsmen Property Group filed a land use application with NYC Department of City Planning to develop 322 residential units across three mixed-use, mixed-income buildings at 156–166 Bowery in Manhattan's Nolita neighborhood. The project includes a 29-story building with 124 affordable apartments for seniors, a 26-story mixed-income tower with 99 units and 3,260 SF of retail, and another 26-story mixed-income building with 99 units and 4,391 SF of retail. The project, designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox and Beyer Blinder Belle, is expected to enter Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP) by year-end.
stories.impact: Nolita (lower Manhattan mixed-income/retail-heavy neighborhood) is absorbing 322 units of new supply spanning affordable-senior and market-rate segments; early-stage ULURP process (EOY entry, 2027+ delivery likely) means this supply will not compete for absorption until 2028–2029; monitor Nolita absorption and rental rate trends in comparable buildings to assess impact on nearby SoHo, Chinatown, and LES multifamily submarkets.
